computer.title: Computer
computer.nothingBody: Open an app window or connect a display, then pull to refresh.

vms.title: Virtual machines
vms.unsupported: VMs don't run on this computer
vms.unsupportedBody: macOS VMs need a Mac with Apple silicon.
vms.turnedOffBody: Agents don't work in VMs until you switch them on.
vms.setupBody: Godmode downloads its own copy of Tart, the free tool that runs macOS VMs. Nothing else on the computer changes.
vms.emptyBody: A VM is a separate Mac for agents: their apps and files stay off this one.

vm.assignFailed: Couldn't change who uses the VM
vm.duplicateShutDown: A paused VM has to be shut down before it can be copied.
vm.resetBody: A fresh disk from {{image}} replaces everything installed in it.
vm.resetKeeps: The shared folder ({{folder}}) and who uses it stay.
vm.deleteCreating: Its download stops and nothing is kept.
vm.deleteManyUsers_one: The {{count}} agent or chat using it loses it.
vm.deleteManyUsers_other: The {{count}} agents, chats and workspaces using it lose it.

command.title: Run a command
command.runsAs: Runs as {{user}} in a login shell, for up to two minutes.
command.label: Command

edit.title: Edit {{name}}
edit.name: Name
edit.diskInvalid: The disk takes a whole number of GB from {{min}} to {{max}}.
edit.diskStop: Stop the VM to make it bigger
edit.diskMin: This image needs a disk of at least {{n}} GB.
edit.diskGrow: CPU, memory and display apply on the next start. The disk can only grow.
edit.bootsLater: Changes apply the next time it starts. The disk grows only while it's stopped.
edit.suspended: A paused VM keeps the hardware it was paused with. Shut it down to change it.
edit.freeUnknown: Free space on the computer is unknown.
edit.tightDownload: Only {{free}} GB free: the download needs about {{download}} GB plus up to {{disk}} GB for the disk.
edit.tightDisk: Only {{free}} GB free: the disk needs up to {{disk}} GB.
edit.downloading: {{image}} downloads first (about {{size}} GB), which takes a while. The list shows how far it is.

vmSettings.isolateDetail: Claude Code's own shell on this computer is off while an agent works in a VM.
vmSettings.fillDetail: Saved logins and 2FA codes, typed by Godmode; agents never see them.
vmSettings.tartPathFooter: Empty: Tart from this computer, else Godmode's own copy. Removing a downloaded image frees space; VMs made from it keep working.
vmSettings.removeImageBody: Frees {{size}}. New VMs from it download it again.
vmSettings.removeImageBodyPlain: New VMs from it download it again.

android.title: Android phones
android.adbCanInstall: adb is Android's free debugging bridge from Google. Godmode installs its own copy (about 16 MB); nothing else on the computer changes.
android.adbManual: Install Android's platform-tools (adb) on the computer, or set its path below.
android.waitingOk: A phone is waiting for your OK
android.waitingConnect: A phone is waiting to connect
android.emptyBody: Turn on USB debugging on an Android phone and plug it into the computer. It shows up here on its own.
android.fillFooter: Godmode types saved logins and 2FA codes into apps on the phone; agents never see them. What is typed on a phone can be read through its shell, so only agents allowed to reveal secrets get this.
android.adbPathFooter: Empty: adb from the Android SDK, PATH or Homebrew, else Godmode's own copy.
android.turnedOffBody: Godmode doesn't look for phones and agents don't use them until you switch this on.

phone.goneBody: It may have been forgotten. Plug it in again and it shows up as a new phone.
phone.name: Name
phone.whatForPlaceholder: Test phone, signed in to the shop's TikTok account
phone.describeFooter: Agents read the name and what it's for when they work with this phone.
phone.assignFailed: Couldn't change who uses the phone
phone.shellHint: Runs with adb shell on the phone, for up to two minutes.
phone.forgetBody: Godmode forgets the phone's name and description.
phone.forgetManyUsers_one: The {{count}} agent or chat using it loses it.
phone.forgetManyUsers_other: The {{count}} agents and chats using it lose it.
phone.forgetRest: Plugged in again, it shows up as a new phone. Nothing on the phone changes.
phone.forgetUnplugFirst: Unplug the phone or disconnect it first.

wifi.title: Connect over Wi-Fi
wifi.pairHint: On the phone: Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code. The phone and the computer have to be on the same network.
wifi.addressHint: The one at the top of the Wireless debugging screen, not the pairing port.
wifi.pairMissing: Enter the pairing address with its port and the six-digit code.
wifi.addressMissing: Enter the phone's IP address with its port.

import.title: Import sessions
import.noChromeBody: Godmode looks for Chrome, Chromium, Edge and Brave on the computer. Cookie exports work in Cookies JSON.
import.keychain: On the computer, macOS may ask for Keychain access so Godmode can read Chrome's cookies. They are only copied into {{name}}. Empty: every site.
import.jsonHint: Paste cookies exported by profile-use, a cookie editor extension or a Playwright storage_state file, or choose the file.
import.tooLarge: Cookie files larger than 20 MB aren't supported.
import.signedIn: Agents using this profile are now signed in to these sites.

assign.title: Workspace
assign.globalHint: Not tied to a workspace; agents use it when they pick it
assign.noProfile: No profile yet: agents browse with {{name}}
assign.noProfileYet: {{name}} has no profile yet, so its agents browse with this one unless they pick their own.
assign.replaces: Replaces {{name}} as the browser its agents use, unless they pick their own.
assign.leaving: {{workspace}}'s agents will browse with {{profile}} instead, unless you make another of its profiles the default.
assign.cookiesStay: Cookies and sessions stay with the profile. Agents that picked it in their own settings keep using it wherever they are.

sync.title: browser-use Cloud sync
sync.footer: Syncs the computer's Chrome cookies to a browser-use Cloud profile, so cloud agents are signed in too.
sync.takesMinutes: This can take a few minutes.
